email_subject: US moves to ban ASML China sales; Samsung delays High-NA EUV to 1nm; SMIC posts record $3B quarter
intro: Washington is pressing the Netherlands to cut off ASML's remaining China business entirely, while Samsung pushes High-NA EUV adoption to its 1nm generation around 2030. Foundry pricing is rising across the board as AI demand tightens capacity.

lead_brief.headline: US presses Netherlands to ban all ASML sales to China
lead_brief.paragraph: The US government is preparing to require the Netherlands to cut off **ASML** — the Dutch company that makes the lithography systems (chip-printing optical machines) that every advanced chipmaker depends on — from selling any equipment to China, according to reporting from NL Times. Separately, the proposed Match Act, which would have mandated US-equivalent export controls within 150 days for US allies or triggered Foreign Direct Product Rule penalties, stalled when the Senate failed to advance the National Defense Authorization Act on July 14, as Democrats blocked the bill partly over its implicit endorsement of the Iran military campaign. That legislative failure gave ASML a near-term reprieve. Under current Dutch policy, ASML cannot ship EUV (extreme ultraviolet, 13.5 nm light) or the most advanced DUV (older 193 nm lithography) systems to China, but it can still sell less-advanced DUV tools and service installed machines at SMIC, Huawei, Hua Hong, and YMTC. A full sales ban would **cut off that remaining revenue stream**, which runs to billions of euros annually, and eliminate the service contracts that keep existing Chinese fabs running. The Dutch government has consistently rejected US unilateral dictation of its export policy, setting up a direct diplomatic confrontation.

briefs.headline: Samsung delays High-NA EUV adoption to its 1nm generation around 2030
briefs.paragraph: **Samsung Electronics** has pushed back its timeline for High-NA EUV lithography (next-generation EUV with higher numerical aperture, which improves resolution by shrinking the minimum printable feature) to its 1nm-class node — roughly the 2030 timeframe — after earlier plans to adopt it at 2nm and 1.4nm. Higher numerical aperture (NA) directly tightens the diffraction-limited resolution, so the delay also defers the tightest patterning capabilities Samsung would have had. **ASML** ships the first High-NA tools, so the delay shifts the demand ramp for those systems.

briefs.headline: SMIC posts record $3B quarter, raises wafer prices into China AI shortage
briefs.paragraph: **SMIC** (China's largest foundry, a chip-for-hire factory) reported its first $3 billion revenue quarter, with sales up 36% year on year and net profit nearly tripling to $479 million. US sanctions have walled off Chinese AI chip buyers from TSMC (Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing, world's largest foundry) and other leading fabs, effectively handing SMIC a captive customer base. Samsung also raised prices by **up to 15%** on new 4nm, 5nm, and 8nm foundry orders in July, with Chinese customers absorbing the largest increases, as AI demand fills advanced capacity globally.

briefs.headline: Micron launches $10 billion US research hub targeting post-DRAM memory
briefs.paragraph: **Micron** announced Micron Research Labs, a Boise-based long-horizon R&D hub backed by **$10 billion** planned over the next decade. The effort targets advanced memory architectures, packaging, and what the company calls post-DRAM and post-NAND compute-memory integration. The lab will operate as an open-innovation model, drawing in university researchers, government partners, and startups alongside Micron's internal teams — a structure aimed at building pre-competitive intellectual property for the AI memory era.

briefs.headline: Nokia acquires NXP's Chandler fab to expand InP optical component output
briefs.paragraph: **Nokia** has agreed to acquire NXP Semiconductors' Chandler, Arizona fab — originally built for RF gallium nitride (GaN) used in 5G base stations — and convert it to manufacture indium phosphide (InP) optical components. Nokia will begin leasing part of the facility in early 2027 and complete the acquisition in Q1 2029, pending regulatory clearance. The move extends the company's InP capacity after its 2025 acquisition of Infinera, which included an InP wafer fab in San Jose. InP-based photonic integrated circuits are increasingly central to **high-speed AI datacenter optical links**.

briefs.headline: LG enters chip packaging lithography with maskless laser direct imaging tool
briefs.paragraph: **LG** has introduced a laser direct imaging (LDI) machine targeting chip packaging interconnects and high-density printed circuit boards. Unlike conventional lithography, which projects light through a photomask, LDI writes patterns directly with a steered laser beam — trading the resolution ceiling of projection optics for **higher throughput and no mask cost**. The tool is aimed at advanced packaging substrates where TSMC's CoWoS (chip-on-wafer-on-substrate, a 2.5D integration platform) capacity remains constrained, opening a market for alternative patterning equipment.

briefs.headline: JCET hits 1.5 µm TSV milestone and reports 79% profit surge on AI demand
briefs.paragraph: Chinese packaging house **JCET Group** completed trial production of a 1.5 µm-diameter, 17 µm-deep through-silicon via (TSV — a vertical copper conductor drilled through a silicon die) with an aspect ratio of 11.3:1, extending its capability toward denser HBM (high-bandwidth memory) stacks and 2.5D/3D integration. The technical advance coincides with a strong financial result: JCET reported **record first-half 2026 revenue**, with profit up 79% as AI infrastructure demand lifted capacity utilization and accelerated the shift to higher-value advanced packaging work.

briefs.headline: Feedforward metrology cuts wafer scrap by adjusting etch after lithography measurement
briefs.paragraph: A process-control approach called feedforward control — where each wafer is measured after lithography (the chip-printing optical step) and the downstream etch recipe is automatically adjusted before that specific wafer reaches the etch chamber — is gaining traction as a yield recovery tool. **Semiverse Solutions** used its SEMulator3D digital-twin simulator to quantify the gain: feedforward control pulled measurably more wafers back within critical-dimension spec compared with traditional feedback loops, which only correct the process after a batch has already drifted out of tolerance. The technique is relevant for any metrology (precision in-line measurement) system feeding real-time data to **etch process controllers**.

briefs.headline: CXMT sought stolen Samsung 18nm DRAM process recipes, Korean court hears
briefs.paragraph: A South Korean court heard that former **Samsung** engineers stole process recipes for the company's 18nm-class DRAM node and planned to sell them to CXMT (China's largest DRAM maker). At least one former Samsung engineer is now in custody. The case highlights a persistent IP-transfer risk alongside the export-control debate: even without advanced lithography equipment, **stolen process know-how** could materially accelerate a Chinese memory maker's development timeline, particularly for mature DRAM nodes already within CXMT's equipment reach.
